title: A graft trigger with no legal target goes on the stack and fizzles instead of not being put on the stack
summary: The designer says a graft composite whose targeted part has no legal target cannot be put on the stack. The RAQ register's own note says the engine reaches the same visible result (no Poison) by putting the item on the stack and fizzling it under the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“An effect fizzles when it loses…”). Then the opponent gets a priority window, and the item can be taxed or negated, though it should never exist. Suspected; not checked against the engine.

title: The engine appears to pass priority to the other player after every action, so a player cannot hold priority
summary: The Manual says a player who acts may keep priority and take further actions before passing. The owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”) and the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“a card played mid-resolution is PLAYED…”) describe the engine handing priority to the other seat whenever an item is pushed. If so, a player can never stack two of their own actions before the opponent may respond (the Manual names Burst as the usual exception, and Burst is handled separately). Suspected from ruling text only; Annex D may record a digital convention that settles it. Measured by the U14 tester: after a battle cast of Luminous Arc, priority is on the other seat, not the caster (pushItem hands it to other(controller)). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: Units played by Wake the Dead and The Bonesculptor spawn in place, never on the stack, and a spell unit they play skips its spell
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“a card played mid-resolution is PLAYED…”) rules that a card played during a resolution is played and goes on the stack, where it can be responded to. The owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“the WIDE play event learns which…”) records that the spawn route used for cards that print "play" (Wake the Dead, The Bonesculptor) predates the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“a card played mid-resolution is PLAYED…”) and still spawns the unit in place, so nobody can answer it. The owner ruling of 2026-08-25 (“"I spawn with N counters" is…”) records that a spell unit raised by Wake the Dead does not cast its spell, though a played spell unit's spell part should happen (RAQ, Hooba-Pon). Suspected still open. Verifier probe (U14 round 1): a unit Wake the Dead plays in battle is in play at once and never on the stack. Affects effects.priority.mid-resolution too. Round 2 probe: onStack=false, inPlay=true; the Wake the Dead comment calls this "the standing playInline approximation", but playInline itself now pushes in battle. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: Bloomcaster does not hear its own play
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“"Whenever you play a unit" includes…”) (current) says Bloomcaster's "Whenever you play a unit" fires on its own arrival when played normally. The verifier measured no 1/1 when Bloomcaster is played from hand: the card listens on cardPlayed from holders in play, and Bloomcaster is on the stack when its own play fires. Either the engine regressed when Bloomcaster moved to cardPlayed (owner rulings of 2026-08-24, “a spell token is a token…” and 2026-08-25, “"I spawn with N counters" is…”), or the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“"Whenever you play a unit" includes…”) is stale and should be superseded (D-U14-11). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: Cards that re-check their target restriction by hand let an earlier part make a later part’s target illegal mid-resolution
summary: The rule (the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“Every target is re-checked against its…”)’s encoding) says target legality is judged once, as the item begins to resolve, so an earlier part of the same item cannot make a later part’s target illegal. markIllegalTargets does judge once, but Minor Kraken (and, by the same pattern, Throw off a Cliff and Leave None Pure) re-checks its printed restriction inside its own run. Measured by the U14 tester: a composite whose first part puts 11 +1/+1 counters on a 0/2 and whose second part is Minor Kraken’s recall does not recall it (control without the counters: recalled). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: Stalwart Sentinel hears its own play from a bin and takes its two counters
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“"Whenever you play a unit" does…”): an ability that triggers when its controller plays a unit does not hear its own card being played (on the stack, not in play). Stalwart Sentinel's '[once] When you play a unit or spell from anywhere other than your hand' listens on 'spawned' with no self-exclusion, so a Sentinel played from a bin by Wake the Dead fires on its own arrival and gets two +1/+1 counters (probe zz-probe-U14-1.test.ts 1b). Bloomcaster is unaffected (it listens on cardPlayed while in play). So the engine follows the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“"Whenever you play a unit" does…”) for Bloomcaster but not for the Sentinel.

evidence.quote: type: 'triggered', events: ['spellPlayed', 'spawned'], bounded: true,   // [once]
A card that is being played is on the stack, not in play, so its own play does not trigger it.

closed: fixed on 2026-10-11 (CT-277, the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“"Whenever you play a unit" does…”)): a unit being played is left out of its own play's listeners, and 444-no-self-hearing-play shows no play listener in the pool, Stalwart Sentinel included, hearing its own play from hand, a cache, a bin or the deck.
